purpose: Guide an audience-aware business document when the requested format does not require a specialized fixed contract, including one-pagers, alignment briefs, proposals, explainers, content-team briefs, and launch notes.
audience: readers inferred from the owner request

ordered_sections.title: Purpose and reader outcome
ordered_sections.purpose: Establish what the reader should understand, decide, align on, or do.

ordered_sections.title: Essential context
ordered_sections.purpose: Give only the background needed by the inferred audience.

ordered_sections.title: Core narrative
ordered_sections.purpose: Develop the main explanation, proposal, update, or argument in the clearest fit-for-purpose structure.

ordered_sections.title: Choices, recommendation, or ask
ordered_sections.purpose: Make a decision, recommendation, requested feedback, or next action explicit when one exists.

ordered_sections.title: Evidence, assumptions, and gaps
ordered_sections.purpose: Use available evidence and identify only consequential uncertainty without creating placeholder-heavy prose.

ordered_sections.title: Next steps
ordered_sections.purpose: Record authorized follow-through or the next discussion when it helps the reader.

narrative_rules: Infer the audience, purpose, reading context, and desired outcome before choosing the outline.
Choose the format, length, headings, and level of detail that best serve the reader; do not force every section into every document.
Start with the takeaway, purpose, proposal, or context the reader needs first.
Use prose for explanation and causality, and use lists or tables only when they improve scanning or comparison.
For non-technical audiences, explain impact and choices before implementation detail.
Ask for clarification only when materially different formats would change the usefulness of the result; otherwise make a bounded planning judgment.
Do not output a template, drafting commentary, source labels, or empty placeholder sections as the document.
evidence_rules: Use only source-supported facts and preserve their evidence state and qualifiers.
Missing data is acceptable in early maturity when it is identified honestly and does not become an invented baseline, target, result, or proof.
A proposed measure can be useful before a baseline or target exists; label it as proposed and state the material gap.
Do not convert a recommendation, assumption, forecast, open question, or dependency into an approved decision or commitment.
Do not invent owners, dates, approvals, classifications, requirements, or document-control values.
terminology_rules: Use terms the inferred audience can understand and define necessary technical language at first use.
Use stable names for products, teams, capabilities, choices, and measures.
Distinguish observed facts, interpretations, proposals, decisions, and commitments.
formatting_rules: Use a descriptive title supported by the request.
Use only headings that contain useful content.
Prefer a brief structure for one-pagers and alignment briefs unless the owner requests detail.
Place supporting detail after the main takeaway or in an appendix only when needed.
Apply the current organization template when the owner or authoritative context supplies one.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, materially strengthened, or assigned a false state.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, approval, requirement, classification, or commitment is silently introduced.
Block publication when the intended purpose or reader outcome is too ambiguous to produce a usable document.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or a material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when drafting instructions, server labels, or repeated placeholders appear as document content.
Block publication when language repair changes protected meaning.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.
